simple.meaning: אַבִּיר (ʼabbîyr) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “angel, bull, chiefest, mighty (one), stout(-hearted), strong (one), valiant.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Judges 5:22. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַבִּיר (H47) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אַבִּיר (ʼabbîyr) / H47 is traced through Judges 5:22, 1 Samuel 21:8, Job 24:22, Job 34:20 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H47. abbir אַבִּיר adjective mighty, valiant — ׳א Job 34:20 + Isa 10:13 Kt (Qr כַּבִּיר ); construct id. 1Sam 21:8 ; plural אַכִּירִים Job 24:22 +; — mighty (always = substantive & in poetry except 1Sam 21:8 ). 1 men Job 24:22 (= violent ) 34:20 ; 1Sam 21:8 (read ׳א הָרָצִים Gr Dr, compare 22:17 ; but Lag Probebibel הָעֲיָרִים אֹבִיל see Id. BN 45 ; Klo גִּבּוֺר ), Lam 1:15 ; לֵב אַבִּירֵי stout of heart Isa 46:12 (= obstinate ) Psa 76:6 . 2 angels Psalm Psa 78:25 (compare 103:20 ). 3 animals ; bull, simile of king of Assyrian Isa 10:13 (read כְּאַבִּיר & see Di); elsewhere plural; metaphor for enemies בָשָׁן אַבִּירֵי ) Psa 22:13 (|| מּרים ); for princes 68:31 ; for Edomites Isa 34:7 ; hence even as sacrificial Psa 50:13 (|| עַתּוּדִים ); of horses Jer 8:16 ; 47:3 ; 50:11 . ** Judg 5:22 ; Jer 46:15 (but 46:15 many MSS. ᵐ5 Aq Symm Theod ᵑ9 many moderns read אַבִּירֶ֑ךָ thy bull , i.e. Apis). אַבְרָהָם see אַבְרָם below II. אבה .

occurrences.englishText: Then the horse hoofs stamped because of the prancing,
David said to Ahimelech, “Isn’t there here under your hand spear or sword? For I have neither brought my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king’s business required haste.”
Yet God preserves the mighty by his power.
In a moment they die, even at midnight.
They open their mouths wide against me,
Will I eat the meat of bulls,
Princes shall come out of Egypt.
At your rebuke, God of Jacob,
Man ate the bread of angels.

For he has said, “By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I have understanding. I have removed the boundaries of the peoples, and have robbed their treasures. Like a valiant man I have brought down their rulers.
The wild oxen will come down with them,
The snorting of his horses is heard from Dan.
Why are your strong ones swept away?
At the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his strong ones,
“The Lord has set at nothing all my mighty men within me.
